same_definition.meaning: B's term is defined by A's
same_definition.reason: a definitional cross-reference is structural (is-a/part-of-like), not causal or temporal

cumulative.reason: plain co-application to the same conduct, with no causal or structural content of its own

complementary.meaning: B adds to A within the same matter
complementary.reason: a co-application relation (B supplements A's own matter), not a cause/effect or containment

alternative.meaning: one or the other applies, by scope
alternative.reason: which instrument governs is determined by a scope/triggering condition — a conditional gate

substitutive.reason: compliance with A is stated to CAUSE (discharge) B's own obligation

separate_tracks.reason: two regimes relate to the same act without one causing or structurally containing the other

non_cumulative.meaning: an express bar on double application, e.g. fines
non_cumulative.reason: an express bar PREVENTS a second legal consequence from arising at all

no_presumption.meaning: compliance with A gives no presumption under B
no_presumption.reason: compliance with A is stated NOT to CAUSE a presumption of compliance under B

defers_to.meaning: A states it is without prejudice to / does not affect B
defers_to.reason: restates which instrument's provisions control — a structural subordination, matching spec §21's own cross_references/savings-clause binding

reference_redirect.meaning: references to X are read as references to Y
reference_redirect.reason: rewires a textual reference from one instrument's identity to another's, matching spec §21's own cross_references binding
